newsitem.title: USA: Enova, PET file Calif. merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Enova, PET file Calif. merger plan.

text.p: Pacific Enterprises and Enova Corp have filed a detailed analysis of their merger plans with state regulators, emphasizing savings for customers as well as other benefits, the companies said Friday.
The companies repeated plans to achieve cost savings of about $1.2 billion over 10 years as a result of the merger, and recommended that the savings be shared equally by customers and shareholders.

Pacific Enterprises, parent of Southern California Gas Co, and Enova, parent of San Diego Gas and Electric Co, announced in October plans to combine, becoming the largest utility, in terms of customer numbers, in the U.S.
The companies also stressed the merger will increase the range of energy-related services and will benefit California by retaining jobs and corporate investment in the state.

The merger has already been formally protested by Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, which is expected to feel the brunt of new competition from the merged gas and electric utility.
Enova and Pacific Enterprises said in the filing that there will be no layoffs of nonunion employees, excluding executives, as a result of the merger.
SDG&E said it has negotiated an agreement with its union for its bargaining unit employees to also receive this guarantee.
Pacific Enterprises' subsidiaries, SoCalGas and Pacific Offshore Pipeline Co, are currently engaged in discussions with their unions.
The companies now estimate that 862 positions will be eliminated rather than the earlier estimate of 1,000 made when the merger was announced in October.
They plan to achieve the reductions through attrition and a voluntary separation program. Some of the affected employees will be offered other opportunities in the merged company.
The companies filed their proxy statement in preliminary form with the Securities and Exchange Commission on November 15 and shareholders are expected to vote on the merger in February.

At the same time, Enova and Pacific Enterprises are seeking approvals from other appropriate agencies, including the Department of Justice, the Federal Trade Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
The companies submitted earlier this month a petition to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, asserting that the proposed merger does not require FERC approval under the Federal Power Act.
The two companies said they expect to receive all necessary approvals for the merger by the end of 1997.
